contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 1 histogram init, 3 per radix pass (histogram, scan internal, state), 2 in the compaction (scan internal, buffer ready), 1 in the final emission (scan internal)
contract.k_range: [1, N) at run time, k == N unsupported
contract.n_range: N = 256 x IPT, IPT >= 1, N <= 32768 (16-bit index and count fields), measured 1024 to 32768
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 (fp16 has traits, outside the focus set), int32 indices derived from the blocked position
contract.nan_behavior: positive NaN orders above +inf and is selected first, negative NaN orders below -inf, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is normalized to +0.0 for ranking (fp32 through one FADD with +0.0, bf16 through a compare and select)
contract.tie_break_support: inherent: positions come from block scans in blocked order, the compacted candidates are in index order and the ties at the k-th key are ranked in index order, so prefer_smaller_index and prefer_larger_index run the same code as not_guaranteed
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

correctness.notes: Every cell passed the full oracle battery for both requirements (random x4 seeds, tie_heavy, sorted_asc, sorted_desc, pivot_tie, all_equal, signed_zero, inf_denorm, quantized_random, relu_quantized). Control is B3_straight in the same lock section. One change: the first digit reads 9 bits (sign plus the whole exponent, 512 bins), later digits 8 bits (fp32 9, 8, 8, 7, bf16 9 and 7).

low_level: The histogram doubles to 512 words (2 KB per buffer), the scan reads two bins per thread in every pass of this variant (the live-bin scan of the tuned variant restores one), zeroing writes two words per thread. Registers unchanged at IPT 4 to 32, bf16 N 16384 latency 155 against 128 (occupancy 1 against 2), fp32 N 32768 spills 804 against 684 bytes.
BAR.SYNC and code size unchanged (25330 against 25298 lines at bf16 N 16384).
algorithmic: The 9-bit digit puts one binade per bucket, so the k = N/16 cells compact 14 percent of the tile instead of taking the fallback (29 percent with 8 bits, above the N/4 capacity, see the host model in T30): N 32768 k 2048 1.268x (bf16) and 1.283x (fp32), N 16384 k 1024 1.149x and 1.238x, N 8192 k 1024 1.036x and 1.181x, N 4096 k 256 0.982x and 1.048x.

Small-k cells (pivot bucket 2.3 percent with either digit) lose 0.90x to 0.99x at N 1024 to 16384 and gain 1.03x at N 32768 bf16: the wider first pass costs about 100 cycles per pass in this variant and the compaction path is entered at N 1024 k 64 where the fallback was cheaper (0.82x there).
negative: At N 1024 the 9-bit digit and the compaction it enables are a loss of 10 to 18 percent, the later tuned variant reverts to 8 bits without compaction below 16 (fp32) or 32 (bf16) items per thread.
surprises: An 8-bit radix digit on normal floats leaves 29 percent of the tile in the pivot bucket exactly in the k/N band of the chunk merges (1/16 to 1/8), a fact that applies to every radix select on float keys and that the B1 cost models did not carry.
open_questions: A 10-bit first digit halves the pivot bucket again (10 percent, host model) at four bins per thread in the scan, untested on the GPU.
Where does the digit9 penalty at small N come from when the live-bin scan recovers nothing (tuned batch)? The compaction entry decision, not the scan width.
